title: Natural quasi-isomorphism before additive total transport
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $C$ be a preadditive category with a zero object and finite coproducts, let $\iota:C\to A$ be fully faithful and additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], and let $\Lambda$ be a left-resolution datum [lem-sfb-left-resolution-reduced-api] for $\iota$ whose functor preserves zero morphisms. For an integer cochain complex $K$ in $A$ whose terms vanish in all sufficiently large degrees [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], form the resolution bicomplex $B_K$ of [lem-sfb-left-resolution-bicomplex-total-exists] and the row bicomplex concentrated in degree $0$, with totals formed from their diagonal coproducts. The total map $\tau_K:\operatorname{Tot}(\iota B_K)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{singleRow}_0(K))$ induced columnwise by the augmentations $\iota R(K^p)\to K^p[0]$ of [lem-sfb-left-resolution-objectwise-cochain] is natural in $K$ and is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the existing construction totalπ' in the source module LeftResolution/CochainComplexMinus.lean. Its HasTotal instances supply the two required totals directly from a bound for K, using hasTotal_of_isStrictlyLE and the elementary single-row coproduct construction. Therefore the separate Sheaf theorem lem-sfb-left-resolution-bicomplex-total-exists is unnecessary. The map itself is total.map of bicomplexπ, which is obtained by applying mapHomologicalComplex to the natural objectwise augmentation of [lem-sfb-left-resolution-objectwise-cochain]. The target row is the singleRow construction of [lem-sfb-left-resolution-single-row-total].

proof.text: For every bounded-above K, use the already proved QuasiIso (Λ.totalπ' K) instance in the source module. Its proof extracts a bound i from K.property, applies [lem-pc-bounded-above-double-complex-total-comparison] with first bound i and second bound 0, and supplies the columnwise QuasiIso instances from [lem-sfb-left-resolution-objectwise-cochain]. This is exactly the first conjunct, without a new comparison theorem or any use of an unproved total-existence wrapper.

For every map φ : K ⟶ L, apply the existing source lemma totalπ'_naturality verbatim. Its two sides are exactly the maps in the second conjunct. This lemma proves naturality by total.map_comp and the bidegreewise augmentation-naturality calculation, with the q ≠ 0 components zero and the q = 0 component the naturality of π. Pair this equation with the quasi-isomorphism from the preceding step using And.intro.

proof_origin.place: E6: reuse totalπ'_naturality (lines 167–198) and the existing QuasiIso (Λ.totalπ' K) instance (lines 200–206); pair their conclusions. The source instances construct the totals without the separate Sheaf total-existence theorem.
